
  ▲ vercel env add name [options]

  Add an Environment Variable                                                   

  Options:

  -e,  --environment <ENVIRONMENT>  Environments to add the variable to;        
                                    repeatable or comma-separated. Prompts when 
                                    omitted                                     
       --force                      Overwrite an existing variable in the same  
                                    environment                                 
       --git-branch <BRANCH>        Set the Git branch for a Preview Environment
                                    Variable                                    
       --guidance                   Show command suggestions after completion   
       --no-sensitive               Store the value as Config                   
       --project <NAME_OR_ID>       Project name or ID (default: linked project)
       --sensitive                  Store the value as a Secret                 
       --type <TYPE>                Set the Environment Variable type (`config` 
                                    or `secret`)                                
       --value <VALUE>              Set the variable value for non-interactive  
                                    use; otherwise use stdin or the prompt      
  -y,  --yes                        Accept default choices when adding an       
                                    Environment Variable                        


  Global Options:

       --cwd <DIR>            Sets the current working directory for a single   
                              run of a command                                  
  -d,  --debug                Debug mode (default: off)                         
  -Q,  --global-config <DIR>  Path to the global `.vercel` directory            
  -h,  --help                 Output usage information                          
  -A,  --local-config <FILE>  Path to the local `vercel.json` file              
       --no-color             No color mode (default: off)                      
       --non-interactive      Run without interactive prompts (default: on when 
                              an agent is detected)                             
  -S,  --scope                Set a custom scope                                
  -t,  --token <TOKEN>        Login token                                       
  -v,  --version              Output the version number                         


  Examples:

  - Add a new variable (prompts for value and Environments)

    $ vercel env add <name>
    $ vercel env add API_TOKEN

  - Add a new Environment Variable to a specific Environment

    $ vercel env add <name> --environment <production | preview | development>
    $ vercel env add DB_PASS --environment production

  - Add one variable to multiple Environments (comma-separated)

    $ vercel env add <name> --environment <environment>[,<environment>]
    $ vercel env add API_URL --environment production,preview,development

  - Override an existing Environment Variable in the same environment (production, preview, development)

    $ vercel env add API_TOKEN --force

  - Add a Config Environment Variable that remains readable later

    $ vercel env add API_TOKEN --no-sensitive

  - Add a new Environment Variable for a specific Environment and Git Branch

    $ vercel env add <name> --environment <production | preview | development> --git-branch <BRANCH>
    $ vercel env add DB_PASS --environment preview --git-branch feat1

  - Add a new Environment Variable from stdin

    $ cat <file> | vercel env add <name> --environment <production | preview | development>
    $ cat ~/.npmrc | vercel env add NPM_RC --environment preview
    $ vercel env add API_URL --environment production < url.txt

  - Add with --value for non-interactive use

    $ vercel env add API_TOKEN --environment production --value "<value>" --yes
